fullPassage: Perhaps nothing has revolutionized the study of human-environment interactions more than the development of spatially explicit methods for collecting and analyzing data. Just a few decades ago, most natural and social scientists collected their data without precise spatial referents. References were made to watersheds, to communities, to villages, to cities, to proximity to rivers, and so on. In some cases (in anthropology mostly), there was even the custom of changing the name of the community and even its location, "to protect the informants." While confidentiality remains an important concern when working with human subjects, the extreme to which this was done was largely unjustified. Everyone knew more or less where these studied communities were, and anyone interested could have found out. Be that as it may, there was very little interest, except in geography, to precisely locate a study area on a map with coordinates. Geography persisted, and finally convinced the rest of us, that place was fundamentally important to understand human-environment dynamics.

questions.passage: Perhaps nothing has (A) the study of human-environment interactions more than the development of spatially (B) methods for collecting and analyzing data. Just a few decades ago, most natural and social scientists collected their data without (C) spatial referents.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 공간적으로 명시적인(explicit) 방법의 개발이 인간-환경 상호작용 연구를 혁신(revolutionized)했으며, 과거 과학자들은 정확한(precise) 공간 지시 대상 없이 데이터를 수집했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① revolutionized — explicit — precise: 원문과 일치
❌ ② implicit(암시적인)은 explicit(명시적인)의 반의어
❌ ③ diminished(감소시켰다)는 revolutionized와 반대
❌ ④ vague(모호한)는 precise(정확한)의 반의어
❌ ⑤ 세 단어 모두 원문과 불일치

questions.passage: While (A) remains an important concern when working with human subjects, the extreme to which this was done was largely (B). Everyone knew more or less where these studied communities were, and anyone interested could have found out. Be that as it may, there was very little interest, except in geography, to precisely locate a study area on a map with coordinates. Geography (C), and finally convinced the rest of us, that place was fundamentally important to understand human-environment dynamics.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 비밀 보호(confidentiality)는 여전히 중요한 문제이지만, 극단적 수준은 정당하지 않았다(unjustified). 지리학은 끈질기게 계속하여(persisted) 장소의 중요성을 다른 분야에 납득시켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① confidentiality — unjustified — persisted: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② justified(정당한)은 unjustified의 반의어
❌ ③ abandoned(포기했다)는 persisted의 반의어
❌ ④ abandoned는 persisted와 반대
❌ ⑤ secrecy(비밀)와 justified, abandoned 모두 부적절
det.tip: confidentiality(비밀 보호), unjustified(정당하지 않은), persist(끈질기게 계속하다)

questions.passage: Perhaps nothing has <u>① revolutionized</u> the study of human-environment interactions more than the development of spatially <u>② explicit</u> methods for collecting and analyzing data. Just a few decades ago, most natural and social scientists collected their data without <u>③ precise</u> spatial referents. While confidentiality remains an important concern when working with human subjects, the extreme to which this was done was largely <u>④ justified</u>. Geography <u>⑤ persisted</u>, and finally convinced the rest of us, that place was fundamentally important to understand human-environment dynamics.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 극단적인 비밀 보호는 정당하지 않았다(unjustified). justified(정당한)는 unjustified의 반의어로, 문맥에 맞지 않습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① revolutionized: 연구를 혁신했다 → 적절
✅ ② explicit: 공간적으로 명시적인 방법 → 적절
✅ ③ precise: 정확한 공간 지시 대상 → 적절
❌ ④ justified(정당한) → unjustified(정당하지 않은): 반의어 교체
✅ ⑤ persisted: 지리학이 끈질기게 계속했다 → 적절

questions.passage: Perhaps nothing has revolutionized the study of human-environment <u>① interactions</u> more than the development of spatially explicit methods for <u>② collecting</u> and analyzing data. While <u>③ confidentiality</u> remains an important <u>④ concern</u> when working with human subjects, Geography persisted, and finally convinced the rest of us, that place was <u>⑤ trivially</u> important to understand human-environment dynamics.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 장소가 인간-환경 역학을 이해하는 데 근본적으로(fundamentally) 중요하다. trivially(사소하게)는 fundamentally의 반의어로 문맥에 맞지 않습니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① interactions: 인간-환경 상호작용 → 적절
✅ ② collecting: 데이터 수집 → 적절
✅ ③ confidentiality: 비밀 보호 → 적절
✅ ④ concern: 중요한 관심사 → 적절
❌ ⑤ trivially(사소하게) → fundamentally(근본적으로): 반의어 교체

questions.passage: While confidentiality remains an important concern when working with human subjects, the extreme to which this was done was largely <u>unjustified</u>.

det.analysis:
